state.case_summary:
A 13-year-old boy presented with an intensely pruritic skin eruption that appeared approximately 24 hours after intensive sun exposure in spring. The patient was otherwise healthy but reported an episode of malaise and headache 2 weeks before first presentation. He had no history of photosensitivity, and denied the use of any topical or systemic photosensitizers.

Erythema and helical thickening as well as numerous small blisters, 2 to 3 mm in diameter, were present on both ears. Similar vesicles were observed at the upper and lower vermillion border. Several erythematous papules and crusts were located on the cheeks, neck, and lower arms.

- Laboratory tests: Differential blood count, routine chemical analysis, and serum porphyrins were unremarkable. Serum parvovirus B19 (PVB19) IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable. Bacterial cultures from blister fluid were unremarkable.- Virologic analyses: Negative results for herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human herpesvirus 6, hepatitis B and C viruses, 8 human polyomaviruses, and enteroviruses. PVB19 DNA was found (viral load of 0.2 PVB19 DNA copies/β-globin gene copy, or 33,438 copies/μg of isolated DNA) in lesional skin biopsy specimen, but not in the serum.- Other tests: Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable.- Images:  Image 1 Title: The Patient's Clinical Findings on the Ears at First Presentation  Image 1 Description: Helical thickening, erythema, and numerous small vesicles are present on both ears  Image 2 Title: The Patient's Facial Lesions  Image 2 Description: Crusted papules and small erosions are located on the cheeks. Several blisters are located at the upper and lower vermillion border
